messages.subject: Questions about point transect intervals
parts:
Hello,



I am a master's student in Brazil and I am trying to analyze data from a
five year point transect sampling. The data was collected

in 216 points, that were located every 200 meters (6 plots of 36 points in
3 different regions, 2 plots in each region).

I have some questions about the software and I wonder if you could help me
by answering whatever is possible from the list below.



Here are the questions:
1 - There were 14 visits in 5 years (the same survey effort for every

point, 3 or 4 visits in a year);

I believe I have to put the number 14 in the sampling fraction, which will
divide (/) the density estimated for 14, right?

And do I have to put the number 14 even if the specie was not registered in
every visits?



2 - Because I need to use the multiplier above, I can=92t stratify the data
in region or year in CDS engine analysis, can I?

So, it is only possible to do global analysis with multipliers in Distance
6.0.



3 - The data is grouped in only 4 intervals and I don=92t have exact
distances (cutpoints: 0-10m, 10-25m, 25-50m and 50-100m).

I've read that the ideal is to have at least 5 or 6 intervals. I'd like to
know if it is possible to have good estimates analyzing these

data with 4 intervals.



4 - I'm reading the user=92s guide, but I still don't understand if I don=
=92t

put a column with the size of the area, it will affect the density
estimated? Considering that the area is the same for each point, and the
same in each plot (1 km=B2).
5 - I don't understand also, if I have to put only the points where the

bird was registered, or if I have to put the points where I have absence
too.
I'm not sure if, when I put only the points where I have records and not
the 216 points sampled in each visit, the program will "understand"
that the animal was there in every visit.
Here is an example of how I am importing the data (in .txt):

year point distance

2005 AV-MA-6-2 75

2005 AV-MA-5-1 75

2005 AV-MA-6-4 37.5

2006 AV-MA-4-4 75

2006 AV-MA-6-1 17.5

2006 AV-MA-1-8 5

2008 AV-MA-4-2 75

2008 AV-MA-2-3 75

...




*OR*



region point distance

ZF2 AV-MA-6-2* 75

ZF2 AV-MA-5-1 75

ZF2 AV-MA-6-4 37.5

ZF2 AV-MA-6-1 17.5

ZF3 AV-MA-4-4 75

ZF3 AV-MA-4-2 75

Ducke AV-MA-1-8 5

Ducke AV-MA-2-3 75

=85
* In this case AV-MA-6-2 is the plot 6 and the point 2 in this plot. Is
there any problem to put the point this way?

Thank you very much for your time and attention and I look forward to
hearing from you.

Regards,


--=20

Nayara Tartari Soto
Bi=F3loga
Programa de P=F3s-Gradua=E7=E3o em Ecologia
Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas da Amaz=F4nia - INPA

Nayara, these issues have mostly been addressed in past exchanges - it is a=
lways worth checking back through past queries.

> > 1 - There were 14 visits in 5 years (the same survey effort for every poi=
nt, 3
> > or 4 visits in a year);
> >=20
> > I believe I have to put the number 14 in the sampling fraction, which wil=
l
> > divide (/) the density estimated for 14, right?
> >=20
> > And do I have to put the number 14 even if the specie was not registered =
in
> > every visits?

Clearly you must include visits when you don't record a species - otherwise=
you will overestimate density. If you want average abundance over the 5 y=
ear period, then effort would be 14 for each point. If you want to estimat=
e abundance separately for each year, then you will have effort of 3 or 4 f=
or each point.
> >=20
> >=20
> >=20
> > 2 - Because I need to use the multiplier above, I can't stratify the data=
in
> > region or year in CDS engine analysis, can I?
> >=20
> > So, it is only possible to do global analysis with multipliers in Distanc=
e 6.0.

See above
> >=20
> >=20
> >=20
> > 3 - The data is grouped in only 4 intervals and I don't have exact distan=
ces
> > (cutpoints: 0-10m, 10-25m, 25-50m and 50-100m).
> >=20
> > I've read that the ideal is to have at least 5 or 6 intervals. I'd like t=
o know if it is
> > possible to have good estimates analyzing these
> >=20
> > data with 4 intervals.

It's possible, if data quality is good.
> >=20
> >=20
> >=20
> > 4 - I'm reading the user's guide, but I still don't understand if I don't=
put a
> > column with the size of the area, it will affect the density estimated?
> > Considering that the area is the same for each point, and the same in eac=
h
> > plot (1 km=B2).

If you don't enter a size of the area, density estimate is unaffected, but =
you won't get an abundance estimate for the area.
> >=20
> >=20
> >=20
> > 5 - I don't understand also, if I have to put only the points where the b=
ird was
> > registered, or if I have to put the points where I have absence too.
> >=20
> > I'm not sure if, when I put only the points where I have records and not =
the
> > 216 points sampled in each visit, the program will "understand"
> >=20
> > that the animal was there in every visit.

The program isn't telepathic - if you visited a point, you must enter that =
point. If there were no detections for a given species, the distance field=
for that species at that point will be left blank, which tells Distance th=
at the point was visited and the number detected was zero.

Steve Buckland
